subject: FinTrust — follow-up: deployment mode & data isolation clarifiers
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintrust.com>, Nadia Park <nadia.park@fintrust.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: FinTrust call recap — deployment mode & next steps

Hi Liam / Nadia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps:

- Current priority: strict data isolation for customer PII and transaction logs (retention 7 years).
- Main constraint: FinTrust wants the inference service to be logically segregated from shared tenant compute and prefers network-level controls for any request/response egress.
- Two deployment modes we discussed: Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools) vs Private VPC (customer VPC with private control plane / optional on-prem connector).

My read from the call: you favor Private VPC for the strongest network isolation but want to confirm which data artifacts would still touch Redwood control plane (billing/metrics) and whether we can route telemetry via your VPC or a negotiated collector.

Attachments: I attached a short matrix comparing "Dedicated" vs "Private VPC" across isolation, control-plane visibility, and typical procurement cadence (redwood-data-isolation-matrix.pdf). Also attached a VPC checklist you can share with infra.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether FinTrust can accept a private control plane (we can offer a customer-managed control plane in the VPC) or whether you need an air-gapped on-prem runtime?
2) Please share the security contact who will run the questionnaire — I can get SAML/KMS/SOC2 evidence over.
3) If you want, I can loop Vivek (SE) and Monica (CS) for an infra-to-infra call to go deeper on routing, KV caching, and acceptable telemetry flows.

Would you be available for a 30-min technical follow-up next week? My availability: Tue/Wed 9–12 PT.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0186

--

Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: FinTrust call recap — deployment mode & next steps

Thanks Camila — useful summary. A few clarifications from my side: 

- FinTrust's default preference is Private VPC with a customer-managed control plane. We want all logs and request metadata to be stored in our S3 (or internal syslog) unless it is strictly needed for platform health.
- Billing/usage: we can accept aggregated usage metrics pushed to our billing collector (no per-request payloads).
- We're not looking to go fully on-prem at this stage; VPC + private control plane meets our needs if KMS integration and SAML are supported.

I've looped security@fintrust.com so our security engineer can validate the checklist and confirm acceptable telemetry windows (they prefer 24–48 hour operational telemetry only). Also copying Nadia (procurement) — she'll run the procurement timeline.

A couple of asks before the tech call:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood's control plane will ever store unredacted request payloads for debugging, and if so what redaction/retention controls exist?
- Do you support customer-managed KMS for model keys and log encryption?

We can do the technical call next Wed 14 Jan at 11:00 AM ET if that works for your team.

Regards,
Liam
Director of Platform Ops, FinTrust

Hi Liam / security team —

Great — thanks for the clarity. To answer your two asks up front:

- Control plane payloads: Redwood does not persist full unredacted request payloads in the control plane for Hosted or Dedicated by default. For Private VPC with a customer-managed control plane, request payloads can remain inside your VPC; Redwood only receives metadata required for billing if you opt-in. For debugging/trace sessions we offer ephemeral redaction workflows (you can request session traces and we produce redacted extracts; retention is configurable and can be limited to 24/48/72 hours).

- KMS: yes — we support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS/HSM) for model keys and for encryption of telemetry exported to your storage. We can document the key rotation policy expectations and support a bring-your-own-key model.

Vivek/Monica — can you join the Wed 14 Jan 11:00 AM ET technical call. Agenda: 1) control-plane flows & network egress, 2) telemetry redaction and retention options, 3) KMS integration steps and proof points (SOC2 evidence). I'll share a short meeting invite with an initial diagram.

Camila

Thanks Camila — good summary and happy to take the tech deep-dive. A few technical bullets ahead of Wed's call so FinTrust has context: 

- Private VPC model: control plane can be deployed inside customer's VPC using a lightweight control-plane connector. All inference requests and KV caches remain in the customer's network boundary; optional usage aggregation is pushed as an encrypted metric bundle to your collector.
- Telemetry: default telemetry includes model version, token counts, request latency. We can suppress request/response bodies in telemetry entirely; debug traces are opt-in and are stored in a configurable S3 bucket in your account with 24/48/72-hour retention.
- KMS/Key management: we support AWS KMS and external HSMs via customer key wrapping; model artifacts at rest are encrypted with customer keys when configured.
- Performance note: Dedicated reserved pools have slightly faster cold-starts for large model families (e.g., >16k context) compared to some VPC connector setups; I'll bring numbers to the call if that matters to your throughput targets.

I'll attach a brief tech one-pager to the invite and bring a sample network diagram. Looking forward to the call.

—
